//: The context is the repo root, so paths in the Dockerfile and in
`output`: wireit then always runs this and Docker's layer cache does
the incremental work. An image is not a file, and `--iidfile` would
let wireit call the script fresh after `docker rmi` deleted the image
This does not depend on `build`. The image runs the site build itself
and .dockerignore excludes `**/_site/`, so a host build is invisible
to it. This builds for the host architecture -- it is for local
testing. Deploys build amd64 in Cloud Build; see cloudbuild.yaml.
--init runs tini as PID 1, which forwards signals to node and reaps it.
serve-static.js also handles SIGTERM/SIGINT itself, which is what makes
Cloud Run shut down cleanly; --init just means Ctrl-C still works here if
--name makes the escape hatch memorable: `docker stop zena-website`.

deploy:setup.//: One time, and idempotent. Enables the APIs, creates the Artifact Registry repository, and grants Cloud Build's service account push access to it -- builds push as that account, not as you, so your own access proves nothing. No `files`/`output`, so it always runs: re-running is the fix when a deploy fails on permissions, and wireit would otherwise skip it.

deploy:image.command: gcloud builds submit --project ${ZENA_GCP_PROJECT:?set ZENA_GCP_PROJECT to the Cloud Run project id} --config cloudbuild.yaml --substitutions _IMAGE=${ZENA_GCP_REGION:-us-central1}-docker.pkg.dev/${ZENA_GCP_PROJECT}/${ZENA_GCP_REPO:-cloud-run-images}/zena-website ../..
deploy:image.//: Builds and pushes only. gcloud uploads the repo root, honouring .gitignore, which comes to about 31MB.

deploy.//: Sends traffic to the new revision. Public unless ZENA_GCP_ALLOW_UNAUTH is set to something other than "true". Use deploy:preview to put a revision up without moving traffic.

deploy:preview.//: Prints a `next---` URL serving the new revision while live traffic stays put. Cloud Run rejects --no-traffic on a service that does not exist yet, so the first deploy has to be `deploy`.

deploy:promote.command: gcloud run services update-traffic zena-website --project ${ZENA_GCP_PROJECT:?set ZENA_GCP_PROJECT to the Cloud Run project id} --region ${ZENA_GCP_REGION:-us-central1} --to-latest --quiet
